comments.text:
I find it interesting that in the timothy short, the first thing timothy notices from the creature is the fact that it doesn't have a mouth, rather than the fact that it is naked. And the fact that us viewers, are likely more unsettled by the creature being naked rather than the fact it doesn't have a mouth (hence what cory said about the creature being more "predatory" than unnatural). This shows that the author played with the situation in such a way that it evokes a sense of childish innocence from the character, while also creating an uneasy environment to viewers (particularly older viewers, who understand that exposing oneself to a child is more concerning than a more visible feature such as a missing mouth.). 
Its like evoking two completely different aspects of human nature at once. It's pretty fascinating!
